Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to velvety brown-black spots on leaf upper surfaces, leaf curling, premature leaf drop, and corky scabs on fruit.
Apple___Apple_scab.favorable_conditions: Cool (13-24°C), wet spring weather with prolonged leaf moisture.
organic_remedies: Spray liquid copper soap or wettable sulfur before bloom and during petal fall.
Apply potassium bicarbonate (Kaligreen) as an active contact fungicide.
Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to eliminate overwintering fungal spores.
chemical_treatments: Apply Myclobutanil (Immunox) or Captan 50 WP during primary infection periods.
Rotate with Mancozeb to prevent fungicide resistance buildup.
prevention: Prune apple trees annually to enhance air circulation and rapid canopy drying.
Plant scab-resistant cultivars such as Liberty, Prima, or Enterprise.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; use targeted ground drip lines.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Small purple flecks on leaves expanding into circular spots with brown margins and tan centers ('frog-eye'); rotten, mummified black fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.favorable_conditions: Warm (24-28°C) humid periods following rains, especially around dead twigs and mummies.
organic_remedies: Remove all mummified fruits and dead wood from trees during dormancy.
Spray copper octanoate or Serenade (Bacillus subtilis) at green tip to petal fall.
chemical_treatments: Apply Captan 80 WDG or Thiophanate-methyl according to local agricultural extension schedules.
prevention: Burn or deeply bury all pruned branches and infected debris.
Maintain tree vigor through balanced fertilization; avoid excessive nitrogen.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae (requires both apple and red cedar/juniper hosts)
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange or reddish circular spots on leaves, surrounded by a red border; tiny tube-like aecia develop on the undersides.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.favorable_conditions: Frequent spring showers with temperatures between 10-24°C when nearby cedar galls produce gelatinous orange horns.
organic_remedies: Apply sulfur-based sprays or neem oil early in the spring as flower buds show pink.
Remove nearby Eastern Red Cedar / Juniper bushes within a 1-mile radius if feasible.
chemical_treatments: Fungicides containing Myclobutanil, Mancozeb, or Propiconazole applied from tight cluster through second cover.
prevention: Select resistant apple varieties (e.g., Redfree, Freedom, Liberty).
Regularly inspect leaves during wet spring transitions.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant green, uniform leaf color without lesions, blight, or discoloration.
Apple___healthy.favorable_conditions: Optimal growth conditions with balanced nutrients and moisture.
organic_remedies: Maintain regular organic compost tea or seaweed extract foliar feeds.
Monitor bi-weekly for early aphid or mite presence.
prevention: Continue balanced N-P-K fertilization, timely pruning, and sanitizing pruning shears.

Corn___Common_rust.symptoms: Golden-brown to cinnamon-brown elongated pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces, erupting powdery spores.
Corn___Common_rust.favorable_conditions: Moderate temperatures (16-25°C) coupled with high relative humidity (>95%) and night dew.
organic_remedies: Apply neem cake extracts or sulfur-based organic dusts early in vegetative stages.
Apply bio-fungicides containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens.
chemical_treatments: Foliar fungicides like Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole or Pyraclostrobin if pustules cover >5% of leaves prior to silking.
prevention: Plant rust-resistant hybrid corn seeds.
Practice early season planting to mature past peak rust spore migrations.

Corn___Gray_leaf_spot.symptoms: Narrow rectangular, tan-to-gray lesions restricted by leaf veins; can blight entire leaves under high pressure.
Corn___Gray_leaf_spot.favorable_conditions: Extended warm (25-32°C), overcast, humid weather with morning fog or heavy dew.
organic_remedies: Encourage rapid residue decomposition with biological inoculants.
Apply copper sulfate pentahydrate formulations during early leaf stages.
chemical_treatments: Triazole and strobilurin class fungicides (e.g., Headline AMP, Quilt Xcel) at tasseling stage (VT/R1).
prevention: Practice 2-year crop rotation with non-host crops like soybean or alfalfa.
Incorporate deep tillage where erosion is not a concern to bury infested residue.

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (2.5 to 15 cm long) starting on lower leaves.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.favorable_conditions: Moderate temperatures (18-27°C) accompanied by heavy dew and wet foliage for 6-18 hours.
organic_remedies: Apply foliar bio-fungicides (Trichoderma harzianum or Bacillus subtilis).
Ensure adequate soil potassium levels to improve natural tissue resistance.
chemical_treatments: Spray Propiconazole or Azoxystrobin if disease is present on the third leaf below the ear leaf at silking.
prevention: Plant hybrids carrying Ht resistance genes.
Till soil post-harvest to speed up corn stover breakdown.

Corn___healthy.symptoms: Robust, deep green leaves with crisp venation and no pustules or necrosis.
Corn___healthy.favorable_conditions: Adequate sunlight, consistent soil moisture, and balanced nitrogen levels.
organic_remedies: Supplement with vermicompost and zinc foliar sprays as needed during V6-V8 stages.
prevention: Keep fields weed-free and scout weekly for cutworm or fall armyworm activity.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Small brown-black spots with characteristic concentric rings ('target board pattern'), usually appearing first on older lower leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.favorable_conditions: Warm temperatures (24-29°C) with alternating wet and dry periods.
organic_remedies: Spray copper hydroxide or copper octanoate every 7-10 days during warm humid spells.
Use bio-control agents like Trichoderma viride as a soil and foliar drench.
chemical_treatments: Preventive sprays of Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb; curative sprays of Boscalid or Difenoconazole.
prevention: Rotate with non-solanaceous crops (avoid planting after tomato, pepper, eggplant).
Ensure balanced soil potassium and nitrogen; avoid plant stress during tuber bulking.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked irregular black/dark-brown lesions on leaves and stems; white fuzzy mildew on leaf undersides in high humidity; foul odor and rapid collapse.
Potato___Late_blight.favorable_conditions: Cool (10-21°C), foggy, persistently wet weather (>90% humidity).
organic_remedies: Apply Bordeaux mixture (copper sulfate + lime) immediately upon early warning.
Immediately rogue out and destroy severely blighted plants to stop airborne spore spread.
chemical_treatments: Systemic fungicides such as Metalaxyl/Mefenoxam, Cymoxanil, or Dimethomorph combined with Mancozeb.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed tubers.
Hill up soil around potato hills (10-15 cm) to protect developing tubers from washing spores.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Lush green foliage without concentric lesions, water-soaked margins, or wilting.
Potato___healthy.favorable_conditions: Cool to moderate temperatures with well-drained, fertile soil.
organic_remedies: Maintain consistent soil moisture without waterlogging.
prevention: Continue preventive monitoring, especially during rainy or misty mornings.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked circular spots on leaves (<3mm) that turn brown with yellow halos; leaves become ragged; scabby black spots on fruit.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.favorable_conditions: Warm (24-30°C) temperatures with driving rains and overhead irrigation.
organic_remedies: Apply copper bactericide combined with microbial bio-agent Bacillus subtilis.
Treat seeds with hot water (50°C for 25 minutes) prior to planting.
chemical_treatments: Fixed copper tank-mixed with Mancozeb (enhances copper efficacy against resistant strains).
prevention: Do not work in tomato fields when foliage is wet.
Sterilize stakes, trellises, and tools with 10% bleach solution.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Target-like concentric ring brown spots on lowest leaves, surrounded by yellowing; stem cankers at soil line; fruit rot at stem attachment.
Tomato___Early_blight.favorable_conditions: Warm temperatures (24-30°C) with frequent rain or overhead sprinkling.
organic_remedies: Apply copper-based fungicides or bio-fungicide Serenade ASO.
Mulch heavily beneath plants with straw or plastic to prevent soil splash-back onto leaves.
chemical_treatments: Apply Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Azoxystrobin at 7-14 day intervals.
prevention: Prune bottom 12 inches of suckers and foliage to avoid soil contact.
Stake tomatoes to promote airflow.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Pale green to water-soaked dark gray/brown greasy lesions on leaves and stems; white fungal sporulation under humid mornings; fruit turns brown and leathery.
Tomato___Late_blight.favorable_conditions: Cool, wet, overcast weather (15-22°C) with persistent humidity >85%.
organic_remedies: Bordeaux mixture or copper octanoate applied preventively before rain events.
Promptly remove and discard entire infected plants in sealed bags; do NOT compost.
prevention: Grow resistant varieties (e.g., Defiant Ph-R, Mountain Merit, Iron Lady).
Avoid planting tomatoes within 100 meters of potato crops.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale greenish-yellow diffuse spots on upper leaf surfaces; olive-green to brown velvety mold growth on the corresponding underside.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.favorable_conditions: High relative humidity (>85%) and moderate temperatures (20-25°C), very common in greenhouses and polyhouses.
organic_remedies: Spray copper sulfate or potassium bicarbonate solutions.
Lower greenhouse humidity with exhaust fans and horizontal airflow.
chemical_treatments: Apply Chlorothalonil or Boscalid if leaf mold spreads to upper canopy.
prevention: Provide wide row spacing (minimum 60 cm) and prune dense foliage.
Drip irrigate early in the morning so greenhouse surfaces dry by nightfall.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots (2-3 mm) with dark brown borders and grayish-white centers, peppered with tiny black fruiting bodies (pycnidia).
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.favorable_conditions: Warm (20-25°C) weather with frequent rainfall or heavy overhead sprinkler use.
organic_remedies: Foliar spray with copper soaps or neem seed oil.
Remove infected bottom leaves as soon as first spots appear.
chemical_treatments: Protective fungicide sprays using Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb on a 7-day schedule.
prevention: Implement a 3-year crop rotation avoiding all nightshade family crops.
Apply 5-8 cm of clean organic mulch around each plant base.

Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Begomovirus transmitted primarily by Silverleaf Whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci)
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Severe plant stunting, erect/bushy growth habit, upward leaf cupping with yellow/chlorotic margins, reduced leaf size, and severe flower drop.
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.favorable_conditions: Warm and dry conditions encouraging massive whitefly populations.
organic_remedies: Install yellow sticky traps (1 trap per 10-15 sq meters) to monitor and trap whiteflies.
Spray horticultural insecticidal soap, neem oil (Azadirachtin), or Beauveria bassiana.
chemical_treatments: Control the whitefly vector using systemic insecticides like Imidacloprid, Acetamiprid, or Spiromesifen.
prevention: Use insect-proof fine mesh netting (50 mesh) in nursery and greenhouse structures.
Plant TYLCV-resistant hybrid varieties (e.g., Tycoon, Securitas, Grandeur).

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Deep green, flat, unblemished leaves with strong turgor and normal flowering.
Tomato___healthy.favorable_conditions: Plenty of sunlight, moderate watering, and balanced fertility.
organic_remedies: Continue routine feeding with balanced compost and bone meal.
prevention: Maintain support stakes, prune lower foliage touching mulch, and water at ground level.
